best_idea: One frame limiter sleeps the rest of a frame period from the measured work time, measures dtime after that sleep, and uses a lower cap when the window is unfocused.
decision_why: Take the two-rate cap (foreground and background) and the wall-clock dtime; in the browser a rAF gate or setTimeout and a visibility-change handler replace the thread sleep and spin; the single-player server coupling is rejected because the server tick stays a fixed step of its own.
acceptance: A Vitest on the limiter: at 30 fps focused and 10 fps unfocused, 10 s of simulated frames gives 300 ± 3 frames focused and 100 ± 2 unfocused; after a 500 ms stall, the next 500 ms run at most 16 frames at 30 fps (no burst).
